name: section
title: Section
description: Full-width page bands with a centered container; the heading that names a band is yours.

when: Building marketing or landing pages from stacked bands.

builtIn: A Section is a landmark; pass aria-labelledby with its heading's id to name it.
youProvide: Heading levels that follow the page outline.

Section.name: tone
Section.description: `default` on ds-surface; `sunken` for an alternate or CTA band. Never two sunken bands in a row.

Section.name: density
Section.description: Vertical padding: ds-space-1000 from 768px and ds-space-600 below; `compact` keeps ds-space-600 throughout.

Section.name: id
Section.description: Anchor target for the Navbar; scrolling to it leaves room for the 56px sticky Navbar.

Section.name: aria-labelledby
Section.description: The id of the heading that names the band (a landmark needs a name to be listed).

Section.name: progressive
Section.description:
Skip painting until the band is near the viewport (`content-visibility: auto` with a 720px
intrinsic size): the content stays in the server HTML (find-in-page and anchors still work),
nothing animates, and the reserved size keeps the layout from shifting.

It also contains the band (layout, paint and style containment): overflowing children are
clipped at its edge, and fixed or floating children position against it instead of the
viewport. So a progressive band holds no fixed, floating or bleeding content (portal overlays
and floating banners to <body>), and the first, above-the-fold band is never progressive. The
720px is a desktop-tuned estimate; once painted, the browser remembers the real height.
